rows.value_as_printed: Detector test facility; no window; internal light source only
rows.quote: We introduce the Michigan Infrared Test Thermal ELT N-band (MITTEN) Cryostat, a new facility for testing infrared detectors ... To minimize external leaks and stray light MITTEN does not have a window for light to enter from the outside: an internal light source is required.
rows.document_title: Bowens et al., The Michigan Infrared Test Thermal ELT N-band (MITTEN) Cryostat (Proc. SPIE 11447, 2020)
rows.reasoning: The paper positively states the facility's purpose (testing infrared detectors) and that it has no optical window, so no external interferometer can view a specimen; its only optics are an internal blackbody source, filter wheel, pinhole plate and Offner relay imaging onto the detector. No interferometer is described anywhere in the full paper. This is a positive description of the instrument's scope, not silence. A 2023 follow-up (arXiv:2306.05470) also describes MITTEN only as a GeoSnap detector test cryostat.

Read the full MITTEN paper (arXiv:2012.06620). It gives detector-mount temporal stability (+/- 0.001 K, not a spatial gradient), a simulated 0.05 K variation across the internal copper light source (not the test specimen), bench 16 K and interior 40 K (different surfaces, not a specimen gradient). No maximum temperature difference across a test specimen is reported. Web search for later MITTEN papers found only the 2023 GeoSnap evaluation (arXiv:2306.05470), which is about detector noise. Tavily was over quota. Not documented-absence because a gradient is a property, not a missing function.

rows.value_as_printed: Detector test cryostat; internal source re-imaged onto detector by Offner relay
rows.quote: a new facility for testing infrared detectors with a focus on mid-infrared (MIR) wavelengths (8-13 microns). ... MITTEN has an internal light source, and soon an accompanying filter wheel and aperture plate, re-imaged onto the detector using an Offner relay.
rows.document_title: Bowens et al., The Michigan Infrared Test Thermal ELT N-band (MITTEN) Cryostat (Proc. SPIE 11447, 2020)
rows.reasoning: The paper positively describes MITTEN as a detector test facility whose internal optics (fixed 1:1 Offner relay) serve only to image an internal source onto the detector under test; it has no window and a 36.3 cm tall x 67 cm diameter working volume. It is not a chamber for cold optical testing of an integrated telescope. Same kind of scope-based absence as the mirror interferometry row.
